summary.headline: Clean Science Q2 FY27: standalone revenue up 11% QoQ to INR226 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 36% as raw material costs rose to 41% of sales.
summary.overview: Management reported a record-high quarterly revenue, with standalone sales of INR226 crore (up 11% QoQ, 10% YoY) and consolidated sales of INR295 crore (up 23% YoY). Standalone EBITDA was INR82 crore (36% margin) and PAT INR55 crore (24%), with margin compression driven by phenol, acetone and methanol costs that were 50-100% higher YoY and could not be passed on to customers. HALS revenue roughly doubled YoY, with around 22% of quarterly sales (about INR66 crore per analyst's calculation, confirmed as "more or less" right) from HALS. Consolidated PAT turned positive in the quarter, helped by a turnaround at CFCL.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (H1 FY27 revenue mix)
segments.commentary: Contributed 77% of year-to-date consolidated sales. Standalone growth was volume-led sequentially and realisation-led YoY.

segments.name: Pharma intermediates (H1 FY27 revenue mix)
segments.commentary: Contributed 14% of year-to-date consolidated sales; volume growth cited across Performance and Pharma.

segments.name: FMCG (H1 FY27 revenue mix)
segments.commentary: Contributed 7% of year-to-date consolidated sales; volumes contributed to sequential growth.

segments.name: HALS (light stabiliser)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2x YoY on strong volume growth; H1 FY27 volumes were 67% of total FY26 volumes. Around 22% of Q2 sales; capacity utilisation about 30-35% (up to 40% cited).

segments.name: Hydroquinone / catechol (CFCL)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 30-35%; output mainly captive, with small sales picking up in Europe and India.

guidance_outlook: HALS utilisation expected to reach 55-60% in the coming few quarters, from about 30-40% now.
Advanced-grade HALS product commercial launch expected in H2 FY27; first shipments to Europe under a contract expected in November or December 2026.
Performance Chemical 2 commercial production targeted in Q4 FY27 (around Jan-Feb 2027); first-year utilisation target 20-25%.
Backward-integration intermediates (ethoxylation precursor started; another intermediate planned next quarter) expected to add 5-7% margin to the affected HALS products.
Management declined to guide on EBITDA margin trajectory given macro and crude uncertainty.
A 1,000-ton line for an advanced HALS grade expected to start by April or May 2027.
capex_capacity: HALS capacity about 11,500 tons now; with NOR collaboration, advanced-grade additions take it to about 12,500 tons.
Performance Chemical 2 expected to commercialise by Q3-Q4 FY27; INR50 crore infused into subsidiary in Q2 and INR150 crore in H1 FY27; total investment in subsidiary INR900 crore.
Little capex currently needed as Performance Chemicals is largely funded; capex for adjacencies to be sized after Board approval of investment case.
Barbituric acid project put on hold: Chinese prices are below what the company can offer, and the other Indian-sourced raw materials have risen almost 3x.
Clean Antioxidant 962 produced at about 500 tons using existing assets, with no separate capex.
demand_pricing: Raw material pressure: phenol, acetone and methanol were 50-100% higher YoY; coal and freight also rose. Raw material cost was 43.3% of sales consolidated vs 39.7% previously.
Pricing: management could not pass through input inflation because Chinese producers are holding prices. Phenol is about INR1,300 in China vs over INR1,550 in India, a gap of at least 10-15%.
Management said it will not be the first to raise prices to avoid losing market share; it would raise prices if customers accepted them.
Demand described as resilient and steady; growth in Q2 came from volumes in Performance, Pharma and FMCG.
HALS: company says it is adding new customers and increasing wallet share with existing ones. Advanced-grade share of HALS portfolio is about 40%, with 770 grade about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA per kg maintained despite the margin fall, and what price hike is needed to restore it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices could not be passed on; absolute EBITDA held up on volume growth. No price-hike estimate was given, as pricing is market-driven and Chinese prices are holding.

qa_highlights.question: What would trigger a price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep testing price increases and will stop when customers push back. It expects competitors to raise prices eventually but does not want to move first.

qa_highlights.question: Will Haldia Petrochemicals' commissioning narrow the phenol price gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so but said the outcome is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration materially lift margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Not significantly. Management estimates a 5-7% margin improvement for the affected HALS products; the main benefit is import-free supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HALS capacity outlook and what is the advanced-grade mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 11,500 tons, rising to about 12,500 tons with added advanced grades. Advanced grade is about 40% of the portfolio, up from a lower share earlier, and the ratio is expected to keep shifting.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Performance Chemical 2 utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to predict beyond a first-year target of 20-25% utilisation, given stabilisation and validation needs.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (phenol, acetone, methanol) with no pass-through; standalone raw material cost at 41% of sales in Q2.
Chinese price discipline and competition, which limits the company's price-raising ability and the margin recovery timeline.
Ramp-up risk for Performance Chemical 2 and the advanced HALS grades, including customer validation and stabilisation.
Barbituric acid project on hold; prospects for new Performance-segment products unclear.
Management gave no EBITDA margin trajectory beyond 60% HALS utilisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, HALS growth and customer trust, but cautious and evasive on margins and pricing: management repeatedly deferred on EBITDA trajectory, price-hike quantum and PC2 revenue ramp, citing crude and macro uncertainty.
key_quotes: So the entire raw material cost increase on account of the inflationary pressure was not translated to the sales growth.
We don't want to lose our market share because gaining these market share again becomes a big problem.
It will not be very significant, but it will be very important for us because then it makes us -- I mean, import-free.

adds.what: Performance Chemical 2 (subsidiary) commercial production, first-year utilisation target 20-25%

growth.why: Management guides HALS utilisation to 55-60% from ~30-40% in coming few quarters, HALS capacity to ~12,500 t with advanced-grade additions, and Performance Chemical 2 commercial production in Jan-Feb 2027 (20-25% first-year utilisation), but gives no revenue growth number and declined to guide margins; backing is partial with a Europe contract for advanced HALS shipments expected Nov-Dec 2026.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 36% as raw material cost rose to 41% of sales (from 35% in Q1 FY27), and management could not pass through phenol/acetone/methanol inflation with Chinese prices holding; it declined to guide on margin trajectory, and backward integration adds only 5-7% margin to affected HALS products.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Performance Chemical 2 (INR900 crore subsidiary investment, INR150 crore infused in H1) targets commercial production in Jan-Feb 2027 (Q4 FY27) with 20-25% first-year utilisation, and a 1,000-ton advanced HALS line is due by April-May 2027, taking HALS capacity from ~11,500 to ~12,500 tons.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: HALS utilisation is about 30-35% (up to 40%) and management guides to 55-60% in the coming few quarters; HALS revenue grew 2x YoY with H1 FY27 volumes already 67% of FY26 volumes, and export share rose to 73% from 64%, with consolidated volume up ~10% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low (HALS ~30-35%, CFCL ~30-35%), so no new capacity capex is needed; management said little capex is needed as Performance Chemicals is largely funded, adjacency capex waits for Board approval, and the barbituric acid project is on hold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to guide on EBITDA margin trajectory and gave no revenue growth number, while raw material inflation of 50-100% YoY is unpassed; no upgrade signal in the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone raw material cost rose to 41% of sales and Chinese price discipline limits pass-through, and PC2 ramp-up and advanced HALS validation carry execution risk on the timelines given.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Advanced-grade HALS commercial launch in H2 FY27 with first Europe shipments expected Nov-Dec 2026 under a contract, and PC2 commercial production targeted Jan-Feb 2027; advanced grade is about 40% of HALS portfolio.

rows.label: Price increases contingent on Chinese price moves
rows.why: Phenol is about INR1,300 in China vs over INR1,550 in India (10-15% gap); management will test price hikes but will not move first and expects competitors to raise prices eventually.

rows.label: Backward integration lifts affected HALS margins
rows.why: Ethoxylation precursor has started and another intermediate is planned next quarter, expected to add 5-7% margin to the affected HALS products, mainly import-free supply.

rows.label: Europe advanced HALS contract shipments
rows.why: First shipments to Europe under a contract are expected in November or December 2026, with export share already at 73% of standalone business.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, HALS growth and customer trust, but cautious and evasive on margins, price-hike quantum and PC2 revenue ramp, citing crude and macro uncertainty; analysts pressed on EBITDA per kg and how much price hike is needed.
